signal: Clearspeed raised a $60M Series D and partnered with Carahsoft to distribute its voice analytics into the public sector

email.body1:
Sean, saw Clearspeed closed a $60M Series D and brought on Carahsoft to push voice analytics deeper into government and defense.

A new distribution channel plus fresh capital usually means more agencies and accounts in play than a sales team can cover before it ramps, and that coverage gap is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Clearspeed off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Sean, quick follow-up for Clearspeed.

Government and defense cycles are long, so coverage matters even more: most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book now to hit the number two quarters out. The gap shows up late, and recovering it is painful.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your government and defense team needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Sean, last bit of proof for Clearspeed.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Clearspeed's reply rate likely compares to other scaling security-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Sean, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling government and defense coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. I know standing up a new public-sector channel takes everything you've got.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a government and defense motion? I'll tailor it to Clearspeed either way.
